title: No input validation specified — undefined behaviour on bad input
expected_feedback: Standard (S3, nature [P] — §8.1: FAIL): the contract does not define what a valid request is, so every client discovers the rules by trial and error and the server has no defensible rejection path. The 500 on a missing email is the symptom; the defect is the missing spec — report it as a design gap, not as an implementation bug. Required: per field, a type, required/optional status, and bounds (`seats` >= 1, `plan` as an enum, `starts_at` as RFC 3339). Which rejection code to use is [D], not [P]: 422 with field-level details is this skill's default, and a consistent 400 is an equally valid house convention — RFC 9110 §15.5.21 does not mandate 422 for validation. What is not acceptable is 500 for caller error.
